correctness.rationale: The real-rank claim is reduced to exact integer 288-by-288 Gram matrices K_d with entry sum_{j=0}^d binom(agreements,j). For d=1,2,3 delivered integer matrices X_d are exactly symmetric, scaled-idempotent with traces giving nullities 263,137,24, and satisfy K_d X_d=0; all identities are independently checked at every entry. Modular Gaussian elimination over prime 1009 yields matching rank lower bounds 25,151,264 and full rank 288 for d=4. Exhaustive row permutations enumerate 288 valid grids, corroborated by a different normalized-board generator. The moment and positivity consequences follow from the constant column and linear nullity; no inference from incomplete enumeration or numerical eigenspectra is used.

value.rationale: The exact hierarchy (1,25,151,264,288) and 24-dimensional cubic moment blind space quantify the order of local statistics necessary and sufficient to identify any distribution on the canonical smallest 4-by-4 Sudoku solution set. This is a natural finite harmonic-sampling benchmark not implied by known solution counts or ordinary four-clue uniqueness; it distinguishes distribution tomography from deterministic completion. No general theorem or noisy stability claim is needed for the exact natural invariant.
